heroHeadline: COLBY TELLS ALL 32 NATO AMBASSADORS IN BRUSSELS LOYALTY QUESTIONNAIRE WAS SENT 'IN THE SPIRIT OF NATO 3.0'; FOREIGN POLICY SAYS DEEP TROOP CUTS NOW UNLIKELY (AUG 27); EASTERN ALLIES OFFER TO CUT US BASE COSTS TO DETER WITHDRAWAL (AUG 21)
heroSubtitle: As of August 28, 2026, the NATO-US tracker's dominant story is the outcome of the Pentagon's Europe force-posture review consultation previewed two days earlier. US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby met the North Atlantic Council at NATO headquarters in Brussels on August 27, briefing all 32 ambassadors on the six-month review he has branded 'NATO 3.0.' Colby confirmed on the record that the controversial allied loyalty questionnaire — leaked by Bloomberg on August 14 and criticized by former officials Karlin and Smith in Defense One on August 23 as eroding rather than building alliance trust — was sent deliberately 'in the spirit of NATO 3.0,' with the review now centered on resolving disputes over base access, basing rights and overflight rather than a blunt troop-drawdown target. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte credited the review process with helping drive a $139 billion increase in 2025 defense spending by European allies and Canada, while Foreign Policy assessed the same day that major US troop reductions are now unlikely — a softer trajectory than the May 26 Der Spiegel leak on prospective jet, bomber, submarine and drone cuts had implied. That briefing followed a Bloomberg report on August 21 that NATO's eastern European members, led by Poland and the Baltic states, are preparing to offer to cover a larger share of the cost of hosting US troops specifically to discourage further withdrawals.
